text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
*Miners of Neves Corvo, southern Portugal, return to work after a week-long strike to protest against a company's measure to impose working shifts seven days a week.
*Portugal looks likely to receive 10 to 20 percent less in European Union aid in the period 2000-06 than during the years 1994-1999.
*Estimates for the first six months of the year show that tax revenues are running 0.3 percent below forecast.

*Crisostomo Teixeira, chairman of CP-Transportes, the part of the newly-dvidided state railway company responsible for operating train services, says that he intends to float it on the market and that the state will assume part of the debt of the company.
*The bank Banif is studying projects in Brasil and Angola, the president of the executive commission of the bank Castro Rocha.

*According to market sources, the biggest Portuguese investment funds, representating two thirds of the national market, will be buyers in the second phase of the privatisation of Spanish electrical company Endesa in October.
